rationale:
Evidence: iteration 10 (score 678.6, best so far) is the iteration 9 design with kd raised from 0.6 to 0.8. Its s-bend progress rose from 0.82 to 0.99 with 19/20 finishes, its slalom progress rose from 0.38 to 0.48, and the oval stayed at 20/20 with 2.13 s finishes. Slalom is still 0/20 (off_track), so the remaining gap is on the tightest bends. Every earlier attempt to raise kp or ki (iterations 3 and 4) hurt the oval, and changes to sensor span (iteration 6) and base_speed away from 1.1 (iterations 7 and 8) also hurt. The only change that has consistently helped in the last steps is damping, with kd moving from 0.6 to 0.8 improving both bend tracks.

Change (one variable, controller only): kd 0.8 -> 0.9. Extra derivative action should keep reducing the lag-driven overshoot that pushes the robot past the 0.06 m limit on slalom. Geometry, kp, ki, base_speed, sensor weights and line_loss match iteration 10, so any change in slalom and s-bend progress can be read as a derivative effect. This is a modest step, since steering_oscillation on the s-bend already rose to about 0.51 at kd 0.8.

Expected result: slalom progress rises toward 0.55 with some finishes, s-bend holds at 18 to 19 of 20 finishes, and oval holds at 20/20. Steering oscillation may rise to about 0.6, which is acceptable if completion improves.

Hypotheses: H1, kd 0.9 raises slalom progress and lowers max_error on the tightest bends. H2, the oval finish rate holds because straight-line behaviour is dominated by kp. H3, if steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.7 without a progress gain, kd has passed its optimum and 0.8 is the best setting.

Next measurements: completion and progress per track (especially slalom finishes), max_error and rms_error (is the lag reduced), steering_oscillation (is derivative action amplifying jitter), line_loss_events, and completion_time.
